20	// TestExitErrorForStatus guards the exit-code contract between this agent and
21	// the executor that watches its Job.
22	//
23	// The executor records a phase success on exit 0 alone (IsJobSucceeded in
24	// agent-task-executor's job_watcher) and never reads the Status this agent
25	// publishes. So a run that reports failure but exits 0 is written as a phase
26	// success, and once the success grace expires the task is parked at
27	// human_review as though a human had parked it deliberately.
28	//
29	// Observed 2026-11-03: task ceb79961 published Status=failed for
30	// "git clone --bare: Failed to connect to github.com port 443", exited 0, and
31	// parked at human_review.
32	func TestExitErrorForStatus(t *testing.T) {
33		ctx := context.Background()
34		phase := domain.TaskPhase("execution")
35	
36		cases := []struct {
37			name    string
38			status  agentlib.AgentStatus
39			wantErr bool
40		}{
41			{
42				name:    "failed must fail the Job so the executor does not record a phase success",
43				status:  agentlib.AgentStatusFailed,
44				wantErr: true,
45			},
46			{
47				name:    "done exits 0",
48				status:  agentlib.AgentStatusDone,
49				wantErr: false,
50			},
51			{
52				name:    "in_progress exits 0",
53				status:  agentlib.AgentStatusInProgress,
54				wantErr: false,
55			},
56			{
57				// needs_input reaches the same park path on purpose: the task is meant
58				// to wait at human_review for an answer, not to be re-driven.
59				name:    "needs_input exits 0 — parking for a human answer is its intent",
60				status:  agentlib.AgentStatusNeedsInput,
61				wantErr: false,
62			},
63		}
64	
65		for _, c := range cases {
66			t.Run(c.name, func(t *testing.T) {
67				err := exitErrorForStatus(ctx, c.status, phase)
68				if c.wantErr && err == nil {
69					t.Fatalf(
70						"status %q: expected a non-nil error, got nil — the Job would exit 0 and the executor would record it as a phase success",
71						c.status,
72					)
73				}
74				if !c.wantErr && err != nil {
75					t.Fatalf("status %q: expected nil, got %v", c.status, err)
76				}
77			})
78		}
79	}

81	// TestPrintRedactsAnthropicAuthToken guards the startup argument dump against
82	// republishing the ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN value into the Job log.
83	//
84	// argument.Print honours only display:"hidden" and display:"length"; every other
85	// tag value falls through to the plaintext branch (`Argument: %s '%v'`). The root
86	// binary's application struct carried display:"password" — a value the printer does
87	// not implement — so each Job start wrote the live model-router credential in
88	// cleartext. This test drives the real printer over the real struct, so removing
89	// the display:"length" tag turns it red.
90	//
91	// Plain testing rather than Ginkgo on purpose: application is unexported, so the
92	// assertion must live in package main, and package main_test (main_test.go) shares
93	// this test binary — where a second RunSpecs fails with "calling RunSpecs more than
94	// once". An internal spec therefore cannot join the existing suite. Same shape as
95	// TestExitErrorForStatus above.
96	func TestPrintRedactsAnthropicAuthToken(t *testing.T) {
97		const sentinel = "sentinel-token-do-not-log-9f3a2b7c1d"
98	
99		var buf bytes.Buffer
100		log.SetOutput(&buf)
101		log.SetFlags(0)
102		defer func() {
103			log.SetOutput(os.Stderr)
104			log.SetFlags(log.LstdFlags)
105		}()
106	
107		if err := argument.Print(context.Background(), &application{AnthropicAuthToken: sentinel}); err != nil {
108			t.Fatalf("print: %v", err)
109		}
110	
111		rendered := buf.String()
112		if got := strings.Count(rendered, sentinel); got != 0 {
113			t.Fatalf(
114				"token value leaked into the argument dump: sentinel appeared %d times\n%s",
115				got,
116				rendered,
117			)
118		}
119		if got := strings.Count(rendered, "AnthropicAuthToken"); got != 1 {
120			t.Fatalf("want the field named exactly once, got %d\n%s", got, rendered)
121		}
122		if !strings.Contains(rendered, "Argument: AnthropicAuthToken length ") {
123			t.Fatalf("want the length form, got:\n%s", rendered)
124		}
125	}

5	// Command github-dark-factory-agent is the canonical AI-heavy agent: one Claude
6	// invocation per phase, all logic in the prompt + allowed tools.
7	//
8	// This binary is the Kafka entry point — spawned as a K8s Job by
9	// task/executor with TASK_CONTENT + TASK_ID + PHASE + KAFKA_BROKERS env.
10	// For local CLI mode (file-based), see cmd/run-task/main.go.
11	//
12	// Reference implementation for AI-heavy agents using the agent framework
13	// (lib.NewAgent + claude.NewAgentStep). Other agents (trade-analysis,
14	// pr-reviewer) follow the same shape — copy this main.go and swap
15	// prompts/tools.
16	package main
17	
18	import (
19		"context"
20		"os"

44	// agentName is the identity string used for Prometheus metric grouping and logging.
45	const agentName = "github-dark-factory-agent"

47	func main() {
48		app := &application{}
49		os.Exit(service.Main(context.Background(), app, &app.SentryDSN, &app.SentryProxy))

56		// Claude Code CLI configuration

58	
59		// Agent directory (contains .claude/ with CLAUDE.md and commands)
60		AgentDir claudelib.AgentDir `required:"false" arg:"agent-dir" env:"AGENT_DIR" usage:"Agent directory with .claude/ config" default:"agent"`
61	
62		// Allowed tools (comma-separated)
63		AllowedToolsRaw string `required:"false" arg:"allowed-tools" env:"ALLOWED_TOOLS" usage:"Comma-separated list of allowed tools"`
64	
65		// Task content from agent pipeline
66		TaskContent string `required:"true" arg:"task-content" env:"TASK_CONTENT" usage:"Raw task markdown from vault"`
67	
68		// Environment context passed to prompt (comma-separated KEY=VALUE pairs)
69		EnvContextRaw string `required:"false" arg:"env-context" env:"ENV_CONTEXT" usage:"Comma-separated KEY=VALUE pairs for prompt context"`
70	
71		// Environment variables passed to Claude CLI process (comma-separated KEY=VALUE pairs).
72		// Use this for ad-hoc / less-common env vars. The three load-bearing Anthropic provider
73		// vars below have dedicated arg slots so they don't have to be packed into this string.
74		ClaudeEnvRaw string `required:"false" arg:"claude-env" env:"CLAUDE_ENV" usage:"Comma-separated KEY=VALUE pairs for Claude CLI environment"`

76		// Anthropic-compatible provider routing. Setting AnthropicBaseURL + AnthropicAuthToken
77		// routes the claude CLI to an alt-provider (e.g. MiniMax via https://api.minimax.io/anthropic).
78		// AnthropicModel drives both the `--model` CLI flag and the ANTHROPIC_MODEL env var seen by
79		// the claude subprocess. Non-empty values override the same keys in ClaudeEnvRaw.
80		AnthropicBaseURL   string                `required:"false" arg:"anthropic-base-url"   env:"ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL"   usage:"Anthropic-compatible API base URL"`
81		AnthropicAuthToken string                `required:"false" arg:"anthropic-auth-token" env:"ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN" usage:"Bearer token for ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL"                                  display:"length"`

100		// token at startup and forwards it to every git/gh subprocess as GH_TOKEN.
101		// The cluster pod sets these (GH_TOKEN is empty there); locally they are
102		// absent and the agent falls back to the raw GhToken above.
103		AppID          int64  `required:"false" arg:"app-id"          env:"APP_ID"          usage:"GitHub App ID (numeric); enables App auth when set with INSTALLATION_ID + PEM"`

109		ReposPath string `required:"false" arg:"repos-path" env:"REPOS_PATH" usage:"Root path for bare-clone cache"   default:"/repos"`

113		KafkaBrokers libkafka.Brokers        `required:"false" arg:"kafka-brokers" env:"KAFKA_BROKERS" usage:"Comma separated list of Kafka brokers"`

120	func (a *application) Run(ctx context.Context, _ libsentry.Client) error {
121		registry := prometheus.NewRegistry()
122		jobMetrics := libmetrics.NewJobMetrics(registry, libtime.NewCurrentDateTime())
123		pusher := push.New(a.PushgatewayURL, libmetrics.BuildJobMetricsName(agentName)).
124			Grouping("agent", agentName).
125			Grouping("task_type", a.TaskType).
126			Collector(registry)
127		defer func() {
128			if err := pusher.PushContext(ctx); err != nil {
129				glog.Warningf("prometheus push failed: %v", err)
130				return
131			}
132			glog.V(2).Infof("prometheus push completed")
133		}()
134		start := libtime.NewCurrentDateTime().Now().Time()
135	
136		glog.V(2).Infof("github-dark-factory-agent started phase=%s", a.Phase)
137	
138		// Resolve the GitHub credential (App IAT or raw GH_TOKEN fallback) and make
139		// it usable by every git/gh subprocess. See prepareAuth.
140		resolvedToken, err := a.prepareAuth(ctx)
141		if err != nil {
142			jobMetrics.RecordRun(agentlib.AgentStatusFailed)
143			jobMetrics.RecordDuration(time.Since(start))
144			return err
145		}
146	
147		deliverer := delivery.NewNoopResultDeliverer()
148		if a.TaskID != "" {
149			if len(a.KafkaBrokers) == 0 {
150				jobMetrics.RecordRun(agentlib.AgentStatusFailed)
151				jobMetrics.RecordDuration(time.Since(start))
152				return errors.Errorf(ctx, "KAFKA_BROKERS must be set when TASK_ID is set")
153			}
154			syncProducer, err := factory.CreateSyncProducer(ctx, a.KafkaBrokers)
155			if err != nil {
156				jobMetrics.RecordRun(agentlib.AgentStatusFailed)
157				jobMetrics.RecordDuration(time.Since(start))
158				return errors.Wrap(ctx, err, "create sync producer")
159			}
160			defer func() {
161				if err := syncProducer.Close(); err != nil {
162					glog.Warningf("close sync producer failed: %v", err)
163				}
164			}()
165			deliverer = factory.CreateKafkaResultDeliverer(
166				syncProducer, a.TopicPrefix, a.TaskID, a.TaskContent,
167				libtime.NewCurrentDateTime(),
168			)
169		}
170	
171		claudeEnv := a.buildClaudeEnv(resolvedToken)
172	
173		repoManager := factory.CreateRepoManager(a.ReposPath, a.WorkPath, resolvedToken)
174		githubClient := factory.CreateGitHubClient(resolvedToken)
175		claudeProber := factory.CreateClaudeProber(a.ClaudeConfigDir)
176		provider := factory.CreateAgentProvider(
177			a.ClaudeConfigDir,
178			a.AgentDir,
179			a.AnthropicModel,
180			resolvedToken,
181			claudeEnv,
182			repoManager,
183			githubClient,
184			claudeProber,
185			// Re-mint before the push: the installation token is minted once here at
186			// startup and expires after 60 minutes, but a lifecycle run routinely
187			// takes longer, so the final push would be refused as an invalid token.
188			a.resolveAuth,
189		)
190		agent, err := provider.Get(ctx, agentlib.TaskType(a.TaskType))
191		if err != nil {
192			jobMetrics.RecordRun(agentlib.AgentStatusFailed)
193			jobMetrics.RecordDuration(time.Since(start))
194			return errors.Wrap(ctx, err, "select agent for task_type")
195		}
196	
197		result, err := agent.Run(ctx, a.Phase, a.TaskContent, deliverer)
198		if err != nil {
199			jobMetrics.RecordRun(agentlib.AgentStatusFailed)
200			jobMetrics.RecordDuration(time.Since(start))
201			return errors.Wrap(ctx, err, "agent run failed")
202		}
203		jobMetrics.RecordRun(result.Status)
204		jobMetrics.RecordDuration(time.Since(start))
205		return finishRun(ctx, result, a.Phase)
206	}
207	
208	// finishRun publishes the agent's result and then decides the Job's exit code.
209	// It exists as one call so Run stays within its funlen budget.
210	func finishRun(
211		ctx context.Context,
212		result *agentlib.Result,
213		phase domain.TaskPhase,
214	) error {
215		if err := agentlib.PrintResult(ctx, result); err != nil {
216			return err
217		}
218		return exitErrorForStatus(ctx, result.Status, phase)
219	}
220	
221	// exitErrorForStatus returns a non-nil error when the agent's published status
222	// must fail the Job, and nil when the Job may exit 0.
223	//
224	// A failed result is still published to the task, but the Job must also exit
225	// non-zero. The executor records a phase success on exit 0 alone (IsJobSucceeded
226	// in agent-task-executor's job_watcher), so returning nil here makes a failed run
227	// indistinguishable from a completed one: the failure is written as a phase
228	// success, and once the success grace expires the task is parked at human_review
229	// as though a human had parked it deliberately (2026-11-03, task ceb79961: a Job
230	// that published Status=failed for a git clone error exited 0 and parked the
231	// task).
232	//
233	// needs_input is deliberately NOT a failure: parking for a human answer is that
234	// status's intent, and it reaches the same park path on purpose.
235	func exitErrorForStatus(
236		ctx context.Context,
237		status agentlib.AgentStatus,
238		phase domain.TaskPhase,
239	) error {
240		if status == agentlib.AgentStatusFailed {
241			return errors.Errorf(
242				ctx,
243				"agent reported status %q for phase %q",
244				status,
245				phase,
246			)
247		}
248		return nil
249	}
250	
251	// buildClaudeEnv assembles the Claude CLI subprocess env from the raw env
252	// pairs plus the Anthropic provider-routing overrides. resolvedToken, when
253	// non-empty, is threaded in as GH_TOKEN — the ai_review phase's Claude
254	// subprocess shells `gh pr view/diff`, and the runner strips pod env to an
255	// allowlist, so the token must be passed explicitly (os.Setenv in prepareAuth
256	// covers the dark-factory daemon path, not the Claude runner).
257	func (a *application) buildClaudeEnv(resolvedToken string) map[string]string {
258		claudeEnv := envparse.KeyValuePairs(a.ClaudeEnvRaw)
259		if claudeEnv == nil {
260			claudeEnv = map[string]string{}
261		}
262		if a.AnthropicBaseURL != "" {
263			claudeEnv["ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL"] = a.AnthropicBaseURL
264		}
265		if a.AnthropicAuthToken != "" {
266			claudeEnv["ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN"] = a.AnthropicAuthToken
267		}
268		if a.AnthropicModel != "" {
269			claudeEnv["ANTHROPIC_MODEL"] = a.AnthropicModel.String()
270		}
271		if resolvedToken != "" {
272			claudeEnv["GH_TOKEN"] = resolvedToken
273		}
274		return claudeEnv
275	}
276	
277	// prepareAuth resolves the GitHub credential and makes it usable by every
278	// git/gh subprocess: it exports GH_TOKEN (covering the dark-factory daemon,
279	// which inherits os.Environ() for its `git push`) and installs git's credential
280	// helper via `gh auth setup-git`. Returns the resolved token for the
281	// RepoManager / GitHub client / gh-token preflight wiring.
282	func (a *application) prepareAuth(ctx context.Context) (string, error) {
283		resolvedToken, err := a.resolveAuth(ctx)
284		if err != nil {
285			return "", err
286		}
287		// resolvedToken is always non-empty here (resolveAuth errors otherwise), but
288		// guard defensively — an empty GH_TOKEN would mislead the daemon subprocess.
289		if resolvedToken != "" {
290			if err := os.Setenv("GH_TOKEN", resolvedToken); err != nil {
291				return "", errors.Wrap(ctx, err, "export GH_TOKEN")
292			}
293		}
294		if err := githubauth.NewGhAuthSetupGit(resolvedToken).Setup(ctx); err != nil {
295			return "", errors.Wrap(ctx, err, "gh auth setup-git")
296		}
297		// A file the daemon re-reads outlives the token bound into gh's helper: the
298		// installation token expires after 60 minutes and the lifecycle daemon keeps
299		// its startup environment, so a long run's own `git fetch` would use a dead
300		// token (2026-11-03, bborbe/trading#433).
301		if err := githubauth.NewFileBackedHelper(resolvedToken).Setup(ctx); err != nil {
302			return "", errors.Wrap(ctx, err, "configure file-backed credential helper")
303		}
304		return resolvedToken, nil
305	}
306	
307	// resolveAuth resolves the GitHub credential forwarded to every git/gh
308	// subprocess. It prefers GitHub App authentication: when APP_ID,
309	// INSTALLATION_ID, and a PEM (file or inline) are all set, it mints a
310	// short-lived installation access token via githubapp.MintIAT. Otherwise it
311	// falls back to the raw GH_TOKEN input — the local cmd/run-task path where the
312	// operator exports `gh auth token`. When neither is configured it returns a
313	// clear error, since the agent cannot clone or push without a credential.
314	//
315	// The token is a runtime value (not a config input), so it is returned to the

# Changelog

All notable changes to this project will be documented in this file.

The format is based on [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.0.0/),
and this project adheres to [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0.html).

## v0.6.2

- fix: link the pinned dark-factory clone to `~/.claude/plugins/marketplaces/dark-factory` so the authoring-rule paths the agents hardcode resolve — a local-path `marketplace add` never creates that directory, so prompt generation ran with no guides

## v0.6.1

- chore: restate the `do-not-merge` gate message to name its bypass actors — the Admin repository role and Integration `3907226`, both `bypass_mode: always` in the `master-protection` ruleset — instead of asserting an unqualified block

## v0.6.0

- feat: **build the release image on a cluster (`BUILD_TARGET=sun`), not only locally.** `make build` had a single arm — a local `docker build` — so publishing a release required a Docker daemon and `docker push` on the workstation. An agent is refused `docker push`, which made a release image unpublishable without a human at the keyboard. `Makefile.docker` now carries two arms, ported from `bborbe/a2a-worker-controller` and `bborbe/agent-claude`: `BUILD_TARGET=local` (the default, unchanged behaviour) and any other value, which renders `hack/build-job.yaml` as a Job on that cluster and pushes from inside it. The vendored `hack/` set is `a2a-worker-controller`'s hardened copy — templated namespace, `case`-based value whitelisting, no service-account token — rather than `agent-claude`'s older one. The cluster arm refuses to run without an explicit `VERSION` (the Makefile default is the newest release tag, so a defaulted build would overwrite a published image with one built from a different commit) and refuses to push a `vX.Y.Z` tag from any `REF` other than that tag. `upload` and `clean` are guarded so a remote build does not fail at a push step for an image that was never local. `Dockerfile` gains a `go mod vendor` step in its build stage: the local arm got `vendor/` from `check-go-mod`, but the cluster arm clones a git ref where `vendor/` is gitignored, so `-mod=vendor` would have failed there. `make precommit` now runs `shellcheck -S warning` over `hack/*.sh`, since those scripts handle the teamvault→Secret credential path

## v0.5.14

- fix: **redact the `AnthropicAuthToken` value from the startup argument dump.** The root binary's `application` struct carried `display:"password"` — a tag the argument printer does not implement. It honours only `display:"hidden"` and `display:"length"`, so every other value fell through to the plaintext branch (`Argument: %s '%v'`) and each Job start wrote the live model-router credential in cleartext into the cluster Job log. The field now carries `display:"length"`, matching the sibling in `cmd/run-task`, so the dump names the key and its length and never the value. A regression spec drives the real printer over the real struct and fails if the redaction is removed

## v0.5.13

- test: **cover the per-prompt setup fetch, not only the push.** `v0.5.12` moved the credential to a file-backed git helper, but only the push site had a regression spec — the fetch site (the one that failed first on 2026-11-03) was pinned by nothing. The new spec starts with token `A`, lets the lifecycle refresher mint `B`, and asserts the credential `git credential fill` resolves *during* the run is `B` — the A→B shape a "file is non-empty" check would not discriminate. No production code changes

## v0.5.12

- fix: **install a file-backed git credential helper so a long lifecycle run never uses an expired token.** The GitHub App installation token lives 60 minutes and is minted once at startup; `gh auth setup-git` binds it into a helper that resolves `GH_TOKEN` from the environment of whatever runs git, and the dark-factory daemon captured that environment when it was started — so no refresh in the parent process can reach it. A token file has no such lifetime: git re-reads it at every credential lookup. Observed 2026-11-03 on `bborbe/trading#433`: token minted 18:10Z, the daemon's own `git fetch origin` refused at 19:15Z with `Invalid username or token. Password authentication is not supported`

## v0.5.11

- fix: **exit non-zero when the agent publishes `Status: failed`.** The result was still published to the task, but the process returned nil, so the Job completed and the executor — which records a phase success on exit 0 alone (`IsJobSucceeded` in `agent-task-executor`'s `job_watcher`) and never reads the published Status — wrote a *phase success* for a run that had failed. Once the success grace expired the task was parked at `human_review` as though a human had parked it deliberately. Observed 2026-11-03 on task `ceb79961`: a Job that published `Status: failed` for `git clone --bare: Failed to connect to github.com port 443` exited 0 and parked the task. `needs_input` is deliberately unchanged — parking for a human answer is that status's intent


## Anti-Pattern: Test-Only Package-Level Mutable State

Same problem as the god object, different shape: production code declares `var X = default` at package level whose only purpose is to let tests override it via a `SetX(d) (restore func())` helper. Often forces a `sync.Mutex` to satisfy `-race`.

```go
// ❌ BAD: test seam leaked into production
var sweepIntervalMu sync.Mutex
var sweepInterval = 60 * time.Second
func getSweepInterval() time.Duration { ... }   // mutex-guarded
func SetSweepInterval(d time.Duration) (restore func()) { ... }  // _test.go
```

```go
// ✅ GOOD: constructor parameter; tests just pass a small value
func NewProcessor(..., sweepInterval time.Duration) Processor { ... }
```

Rule: configurable values that vary between production and tests are **constructor parameters**, not package vars. The default lives in `main.go` / the factory, not at package scope.
